analysis.summary_en: You have received a formal Show Cause Notice in Form GST DRC-01 under Section 73 of the CGST Act for financial year 2022-23. The tax authority alleges that your outward turnover reported in GSTR-3B is lower than your e-Way Bill generated values, demanding differential tax of Rs. 5,80,000 along with applicable interest under Section 50 and 10% penalty. This is a substantive demand notice requiring a formal legal defence. Under Rule 142(4), your response must be filed in Form GST DRC-06 within 30 days. Factual explanations detailing cancelled e-way bills or non-sales transport movements must be substantiated with documentary logs.
analysis.summary_hi: आपको वित्तीय वर्ष 2022-23 के लिए सीजीएसटी अधिनियम की धारा 73 के तहत फॉर्म GST DRC-01 में कारण बताओ नोटिस (Show Cause Notice) प्राप्त हुआ है। कर विभाग का आरोप है कि आपके GSTR-3B में घोषित बिक्री कारोबार (Turnover), ई-वे बिल के कुल मूल्य से कम है, जिसके आधार पर ₹5,80,000 का कर, धारा 50 के तहत ब्याज और ₹58,000 का जुर्माना मांगा गया है। यह एक गंभीर मांग नोटिस है जिसका औपचारिक कानूनी जवाब देना अनिवार्य है। नियम 142(4) के तहत आपको 30 दिनों के भीतर फॉर्म GST DRC-06 में अपना उत्तर देना होगा। रद्द किए गए ई-वे बिल और गैर-बिक्री स्टॉक ट्रांसफर के प्रमाण प्रस्तुत करके इस मांग का समाधान किया जा सकता है।

draft.body_md:
# REPLY TO SHOW CAUSE NOTICE UNDER SECTION 73 (FORM GST DRC-06)

**To:**
The Deputy Commissioner,
Sector 4, Surat Commissionerate,
Gujarat

**Subject:** Reply to Show Cause Notice issued under Section 73 in Form GST DRC-01 bearing Ref: GST/GJ/SURAT/DRC-01/2026/4109 dated 12-10-2026

**GSTIN:** 24AAEFK4312Q1ZX  
**Taxpayer Name:** Kalyan Textiles Trading LLP  
**Financial Year:** 2022-23  

---

Respected Sir,

### 1. Preliminary Submissions
1. At the outset, the noticee denies all allegations, proposed tax demands of Rs. 5,80,000/-, interest under Section 50, and penalty proposed under Section 73(9) [[cgst-act-s73#p9]] as erroneous and unsustainable in law and on facts.
2. This representation in Form GST DRC-06 is submitted within the thirty-day limitation window pursuant to Rule 142(4) of the CGST Rules, 2017 [[cgst-rules-r142#p1]].

### 2. Detailed Defence on Alleged Turnover Variance
**Allegation:** Under-reporting of outward supplies in GSTR-3B by Rs. 32,22,222/- when compared with e-Way bill generated values.

**Noticee's Submissions:**
1. It is submitted that e-Way bills generated do not equate to taxable supplies per se. As contemplated under the scheme of Section 73(1) [[cgst-act-s73#p1]], tax liability arises solely on supplies within the meaning of Section 7.
2. During FY 2022-23, certain e-Way bills were generated for movements involving job-work and inter-branch transfers that did not involve any taxable outward consideration [ADD: List of delivery challan numbers and job-worker registration details].
3. Furthermore, multiple e-Way bills were cancelled within the portal window due to vehicle breakdowns and order cancellations [ADD: Cancelled e-Way bill numbers and corresponding credit note entries].
4. All genuine outward sales have been duly declared in Form GSTR-1 and discharge of tax was fully accounted for in Form GSTR-3B [ADD: CA audited turnover reconciliation certificate reference].

### 3. Non-Applicability of Penalty
Since the noticee has not short-paid tax with any willful intention, the levy of penalty under Section 73(9) [[cgst-act-s73#p9]] is wholly unwarranted.

### 4. Prayer
In view of the above submissions, the noticee respectfully prays:
a) That the proposed demand of tax, interest, and penalty under Section 73 [[cgst-act-s73#p1]] be dropped in toto;
b) That an order in Form GST DRC-05 concluding the proceedings be issued;
c) That a personal hearing be granted before passing any adverse adjudication order.

---

### 5. Enclosures
1. Reconciliation table between e-Way Bills and GSTR-3B turnover.
2. Job-work delivery challans and transport consignment notes.
3. Log of cancelled e-Way bills.
4. [ADD: Bank statements and audited financial statements for FY 2022-23].

Yours faithfully,

For **Kalyan Textiles Trading LLP**



__________________________________  
**Designated Partner / Authorized Signatory**  
Date: [Date of Reply Submission]

cgst-act-s73#p1.content: Where it appears to the proper officer that any tax has not been paid or short paid or erroneously refunded, or where input tax credit has been wrongly availed or utilised for any reason, other than the reason of fraud or any wilful-misstatement or suppression of facts to evade tax, he shall serve notice on the person chargeable with tax which has not been so paid or which has been short paid or to whom the refund has erroneously been made, or who has wrongly availed or utilised input tax credit, requiring him to show cause as to why he should not pay the amount specified in the notice along with interest payable thereon under section 50 and a penalty leviable under the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder.

cgst-act-s73#p9.content: The proper officer shall, after considering the representation, if any, made by person chargeable with tax, determine the amount of tax, interest and a penalty equivalent to ten per cent. of tax or ten thousand rupees, whichever is higher, due from such person and issue an order.

cgst-rules-r142#p1.content: The representation referred to in sub-section (9) of section 73 or sub-section (9) of section 74 or sub-section (3) of section 76 or the reply to any notice issued under any other section shall be in FORM GST DRC-06.
